need: Every caller that masks text, JSON or log records builds one Scanner with the detectors and threshold its data needs and shares it across goroutines.
without: Without a constructor each call site would have to pass the kind list and threshold to every Mask, slog and adapter call, and could not share the compiled dispatch tables.

need: Handlers, adapters, embargotest and the CLI all take the same *Scanner so one configuration decides what is masked everywhere in a program.
without: Without a shared type each hook would take its own option list, and a team could configure the HTTP log and the slog handler differently by mistake.

need: NewScanner takes a sealed option type so callers choose kinds, threshold, custom detectors and sensitive keys in one call that later options cannot break.
without: Without an option type NewScanner would need a config struct whose zero values are ambiguous (zero threshold versus unset) and whose fields could not be validated in one place.

need: A service that handles only email and cards selects those kinds, which removes false positives from unrelated detectors and lowers the scan cost.
without: Without it a caller could only use the default 26 kinds and would filter findings afterwards, paying for every detector and still masking with WithAll's opt-in kinds unavailable.

need: A service in one country keeps NewScanner's default and turns on that country's formats, such as My Number and Japanese phone numbers, which are opt-in.
without: Without it the caller would list all 19 default kinds in WithKinds plus its own, and that copied list would not follow later changes to the default.

need: A service that stores identifiers from several countries enables every national ID kind and the entropy heuristic in one option, including kinds added in later releases.
without: Without it the caller would list all 38 kinds in WithKinds and would silently miss any kind a later release adds.

need: A team that sees too many low-score findings, such as labeled business numbers or lower-scored bank accounts, drops them below a threshold it chose from doc/accuracy.md.
without: Without it every caller of Scan would filter Confidence by hand, and the slog handler, MaskJSON and adapters, which mask internally, could not be tuned at all.

need: A support team that must match a card or account to a customer keeps the last four digits in log records and MaskJSON output, while every other kind stays hidden.
without: Without it partial display worked only on text passed to MaskFunc, so a team that wanted it in logs would drop the slog handler and the adapters and lose their key and structure rules.

need: An application with its own identifier format, such as an internal customer number, adds a detector that every hook and embargotest then uses like a built-in.
without: Without it the application would mask its own format in a separate pass after each hook, and slog, MaskJSON and the adapters would never see the custom kind.

need: A team whose payloads name secrets with its own keys, such as x_partner_sig, adds those keys so values under them are hidden whatever they contain, keeping the default names.
without: Without it values under unusual key names would be masked only when a detector recognized the value, and opaque signatures that match no detector would leak.

need: A team whose API returns a public pagination cursor named token, or whose export must hide exactly the keys a contract lists, drops the default names and suffix rule.
without: Without it every value under token, secret or a *_password key is replaced, so the team would post-process the masked output or stop using the structured masking.

need: An application that implements WithDetector needs the method set its custom detector must satisfy, and the documented contract for spans and scores.
without: Without a named interface WithDetector would take a bare function and the contract (terminate, no mutation, valid spans) would have nowhere to be documented.

need: A custom detector returns its findings for one input; this is the single method the scanner calls on it.
without: Without a method on the interface there would be no way for the scanner to call the custom detector on the caller's original bytes.

need: Callers of Scan need each match's kind, byte range and score to mask, count or report it, as the audit CLI and custom report code do.
without: Without a result type Scan could only return masked text, and callers could not count by kind, keep some kinds visible or write their own report.

need: Callers of Scan read Finding.Kind to group findings by kind, keep a kind visible or report counts per kind.
without: Without the field the caller would have to rescan or reparse the matched text to recover the same information, which the detector already computed.

need: Callers of Scan read Finding.Start to slice the original input, highlight the match or report a column without copying the value.
without: Without the field the caller would have to rescan or reparse the matched text to recover the same information, which the detector already computed.

need: Callers of Scan read Finding.End to slice the original input and know where the match stops, which Mask needs to merge overlaps.
without: Without the field the caller would have to rescan or reparse the matched text to recover the same information, which the detector already computed.

need: Callers of Scan read Finding.Confidence to apply their own threshold per kind or show how certain a match is, as doc/audit.md does.
without: Without the field the caller would have to rescan or reparse the matched text to recover the same information, which the detector already computed.

need: Findings, WithKinds, WithAllowedKinds and custom detectors all name a detector by a typed string so a typo in a kind fails WithKinds instead of matching nothing.
without: Without a named type kinds would be plain strings and a misspelled kind passed to WithKinds or WithAllowedKinds would silently select nothing.

need: Each constant names one built-in detector so a caller can select it in WithKinds, allow it in embargotest or compare Finding.Kind against it.
without: Without constants callers would type the string values, and a renamed or misspelled kind would compile and then select or allow nothing.

need: Code that already holds bytes, such as a request body or a buffered log line, gets the findings without converting to a string.
without: Without it the caller would convert to a string for ScanString, copying the input on every call in the hot path of a log writer.

need: Code that holds a string, such as an error message or a formatted log line, gets the findings for Mask with the same offsets it will slice.
without: Without it each caller would write scanner.Scan([]byte(s)); the conversion is the same, but every text example would start with a byte-slice conversion that has nothing to do with masking.

need: A program that audits a log file or a stream reports each finding with its line number without loading the whole input or splitting lines itself.
without: Without it the caller would write a bufio loop, handle CRLF, long lines and PEM blocks that span lines, which ScanLines already gets right.

need: Code that sends JSON to a support system, an audit export or an API log masks it while keeping keys, numbers, booleans and nesting.
without: Without it the caller would decode into any, walk the tree, scan each string and re-encode, and would lose number precision and key order on the way.

need: Request-scoped work, such as masking a large response body in an HTTP middleware or OpenTelemetry export, stops when the request or export is cancelled.
without: Without it a cancelled request would keep scanning a large document to the end, and the OpenTelemetry adapter could not honour the exporter's deadline.

need: Code that writes a log line or error message replaces every finding with [REDACTED], merging overlapping spans correctly.
without: Without it every caller would sort findings, merge overlaps and handle invalid ranges itself, and a wrong merge would print part of a secret.

need: A team that must keep a different marker per kind, such as [EMAIL] or a hash for joining records, replaces each merged span through its own function.
without: Without it the team would reimplement the overlap merge of Mask to write its own marker, and a mistake there prints part of the secret.

need: A service that logs through log/slog wraps its existing handler so structs, errors and strings are masked while keys, types and nesting stay the same.
without: Without it every log call would wrap values by hand, and any field added later to a logged struct would be printed until someone remembered to mask it.

need: A net/http server writes one access log record per request with tokens and personal data masked in the path, query and headers.
without: Without it the server would build its own access log middleware and mask the request line itself, which is where reset tokens and emails usually leak.

need: Code that loads an API key or password wraps it once so fmt, JSON, XML, templates and loggers print [REDACTED] instead of the value.
without: Without it the value would be a plain string and any log call, error wrap or %+v of the enclosing struct would print it.

need: Structs that hold a credential declare the field as Secret[string] so the type itself prevents printing, including inside unexported fields.
without: Without a type the struct field would be a string and printing the struct, or marshalling it to JSON, would expose the credential.

need: The one place that needs the real credential, such as an HTTP client setting a header, reads it explicitly and visibly in code review.
without: Without it the value could not be read back at all, or it would need an accessor whose name hides that the secret leaves its wrapper.

need: A request or config DTO declares a field as Input[string] so the decoded password or token is a Secret from the moment it is read.
without: Without it the DTO would decode into a string field and the plain value would live in the struct, where a log of the request prints it.

need: After decoding a DTO, the handler takes the decoded value as a Secret to pass on, which is the only way to get the value out of Input.
without: Without it the decoded value would be unreachable, or Input would need Reveal and the explicit hand-off to a Secret would be lost.

need: fmt calls Format for every verb, including %v, %s, %q, %x and %#v, when a program prints a Secret or a struct holding one.
without: Without it fmt would print the wrapped value through its default formatting, which is the leak Secret exists to prevent.

need: text/template, html/template and code that asks for fmt.Stringer, such as error wrappers and some loggers, call String when they print a Secret.
without: Without it those callers would fall back to the default formatting of the wrapped value.

need: log/slog calls LogValue when a Secret is an attribute value, so the record carries the marker before any handler sees it.
without: Without it slog would format the wrapped value through reflection in each handler, which is the leak Secret exists to prevent.

need: encoding/json calls MarshalJSON when a Secret, or a struct or map holding one, is marshaled for a response, a config dump or a JSON log.
without: Without it encoding/json would marshal the wrapped value itself.

need: encoding/xml, map keys in encoding/json and text-based encoders call MarshalText when they write a Secret.
without: Without it those encoders would write the wrapped value or fail on the type.

need: fmt calls Format for every verb, including %v, %s, %q, %x and %#v, when a program prints a Input or a struct holding one.
without: Without it fmt would print the wrapped value through its default formatting, which is the leak Input exists to prevent.

need: text/template, html/template and code that asks for fmt.Stringer, such as error wrappers and some loggers, call String when they print a Input.
without: Without it those callers would fall back to the default formatting of the wrapped value.

need: log/slog calls LogValue when a Input is an attribute value, so the record carries the marker before any handler sees it.
without: Without it slog would format the wrapped value through reflection in each handler, which is the leak Input exists to prevent.

need: encoding/json calls MarshalJSON when a Input, or a struct or map holding one, is marshaled for a response, a config dump or a JSON log.
without: Without it encoding/json would marshal the wrapped value itself.

need: encoding/xml, map keys in encoding/json and text-based encoders call MarshalText when they write a Input.
without: Without it those encoders would write the wrapped value or fail on the type.

need: encoding/json calls this method when a request body or config file is decoded into a DTO with an Input field, so the value goes straight into a Secret.
without: Without it the JSON decoder could not fill an Input field and the DTO would need a plain string field that holds the secret in the clear.

need: Text decoders such as encoding/xml attributes, flag values and environment config libraries call this method to fill an Input from a string.
without: Without it those decoders could not fill an Input field and the secret would be read into a plain string first.

need: database/sql calls this method when a row column is scanned into an Input, so a stored token or password is a Secret as soon as it is read.
without: Without it the caller would scan into a string or []byte, which the driver may reuse, and wrap it by hand after the plain value already existed.

need: A test creates a Recorder that holds a fake canary secret and captures every output the code under test writes, then checks that the canary never appears.
without: Without it a test would plant its own fake secret, capture each output by hand and search them, and would miss encoded or split forms the Recorder checks.

need: Tests pass the Recorder's writers, HTTP recorder and canary to the code under test and call Check at the end; the type holds that state.
without: Without a type the captures and canary would be loose variables and the test could not attach expectations or one final check.

need: New and Guard take sealed options so a test changes the canary, scanner, allowances and limits in one call that is validated at once.
without: Without an option type New would need a config struct whose zero values are ambiguous, such as zero bytes meaning unlimited or unset.

need: The test passes the fake secret into the code under test through any input, such as t.Setenv, a header or a request body.
without: Without it the test could not feed the Recorder's canary into the code, and would invent its own value that the Recorder does not search for.

need: The test gives the code under test a named io.Writer as its log or stdout sink, so its output is captured and searched for the canary.
without: Without it the test would capture output in a bytes.Buffer and search it itself, missing the escaped, encoded and split forms the Recorder checks.

need: A handler test writes the response into a named recorder so status, headers, body and trailers are all searched for the canary.
without: Without it the test would use httptest.ResponseRecorder and check the body only, and secrets in headers or trailers would pass.

need: Code that leaks through a child process, os.Exit or a panic is run as a helper in a child so its real stdout and stderr are searched.
without: Without it the test could not capture output written after the process exits or panics, which is where crash dumps print secrets.

need: A test also requires that the useful diagnostic, such as an error code, reached the sink, so masking that removes everything fails.
without: Without it a test that passes because the log is empty would look the same as one that logged a masked record, and over-masking would go unnoticed.

need: A test of JSON logs requires count records at a path with given field values, such as {"code": "signing_failed"}, so the record survived masking.
without: Without it the test would parse NDJSON by hand inside Expect for each log assertion, which every structured-log test needs.

need: The test ends with one call that searches every capture for the canary and other findings and fails with the leaking sink named.
without: Without it there would be no point where the captures are complete and searched, and leaks in late writes would be missed.

need: A package's TestMain runs every test under a supervisor that searches real stdout, stderr, t.Log and panics for findings, without changing each test.
without: Without it each test would need its own Recorder and still could not see output written by t.Log, panics or goroutines that outlive the test.

need: A test checks that a type holding a secret, such as a config struct, prints no canary through fmt, JSON, XML, templates, slog or wrapped errors.
without: Without it the test would print the value through each of those paths itself and would likely skip XML, templates or error wrapping.

need: A test whose code validates input format, such as a key with a fixed prefix, supplies its own fake canary that the code accepts.
without: Without it the Recorder's fixed default canary would be rejected by the code under test, and the test could not reach the logging path.

need: A test checks output with the same Scanner configuration the application uses, such as opt-in national IDs or a custom detector.
without: Without it the Recorder would search with the default 26 kinds only and would miss leaks of kinds the application enabled.

need: A test whose fixtures contain fake data of a kind, such as sample IP addresses in access logs, stops those findings from failing the check.
without: Without it every test with realistic fixtures would fail on findings that are not leaks, and teams would turn the check off.

need: A test allows exact fixture values, such as a documented sample email, while other findings of the same kind still fail.
without: Without it the test could only allow the whole kind through WithAllowedKinds and would then miss a real leak of that kind.

need: A test of code that truncates or splits values across lines also fails when a long piece of the canary appears.
without: Without it a log that prints the first 40 bytes of a token, or one half per line, would pass because the whole canary never appears.

need: A test that produces large output raises the capture limit, or a memory-bound test lowers it, without changing the timeout.
without: Without it the test would hit the default capture limit and fail on truncation, with no way to raise only that bound.

need: A test whose child process under Run or test binary under Guard runs long raises the deadline, or a fast suite lowers it, without changing the capture limit.
without: Without it a slow child would be stopped at the default deadline, with no way to raise only that bound; in-process code is not interrupted either way.

need: A service that logs through zap wraps its WriteSyncer so every encoded entry is masked before it is written, with no change to log calls.
without: Without it the service would write its own WriteSyncer that parses each JSON entry, masks it and forwards it, or move its logging to slog.

need: A service that logs through zerolog wraps its output writer so every JSON event is masked before it is written, with no change to log calls.
without: Without it the service would write its own io.Writer that splits events, masks them and forwards them, or move its logging to slog.

need: A service that logs through logrus wraps its formatter so every entry is masked after formatting, with no change to log calls.
without: Without it the service would write its own logrus.Formatter that masks fields and messages, or move its logging to slog.

need: A gRPC server logs one masked record per unary call, with tokens and personal data in metadata and errors hidden.
without: Without it the server would write its own interceptor and mask metadata and status messages, which is where bearer tokens usually leak.

need: A gRPC server logs one masked record per streaming call, with tokens and personal data in metadata and errors hidden.
without: Without it the server would write its own stream interceptor and mask metadata and status messages, which is where bearer tokens usually leak.

need: A service that exports logs through the OpenTelemetry SDK masks each record's body and attributes before they leave the process.
without: Without it the service would wrap the exporter itself and walk every log record value, or rely on a collector after the data has left the process.

need: A service that exports traces masks span names, attributes, events and status messages, where SQL text and URLs often carry secrets.
without: Without it the service would wrap the span exporter itself and copy every read-only span to mask it, which the SDK makes awkward.

need: A service that reports errors to Sentry masks each event's message, exception, breadcrumbs, request and extra data before it is sent.
without: Without it the service would write its own BeforeSend that walks every event field, and new fields Sentry adds would leak until it was updated.

need: An LLM agent or CI step picks the masked text, a summary document or one JSON object per finding with a single flag instead of one flag per output.
without: Without it the command would need a separate flag for each output, as --report was, and a script could not ask for per-finding JSON lines at all.

need: An audit of one log source checks only the kinds that source can hold, or adds the opt-in national IDs with all, matching WithKinds in the library.
without: Without it the command would always run the default 26 kinds, and an audit could not include the opt-in kinds or exclude noisy ones.

need: An audit that wants only strong findings drops low-score ones, matching WithMinConfidence, before counting or failing a CI step.
without: Without it every script would filter the JSON output by confidence itself, and the default text output could not be tuned at all.

need: A json report shows up to N locations per kind so a reviewer can open the lines, or zero for counts only in a CI log.
without: Without it the report would always print a fixed number of locations, too many for a CI log or too few to review a noisy kind.

need: A bug report or CI log records which release of the command produced the output, since detection changes between minor versions.
without: Without it a user could not tell which detector rules produced a finding, and go version -m on the binary is not something users know.

need: A user or an LLM agent reads the flags, formats and input rules from the command itself before running it on real logs.
without: Without it the only documentation would be the README, which an agent in a shell or an offline machine may not have.
